Week 3: More about margins of error

____
Published

September 11, 2026

Why plot data?

  • Ansombe’s Quartet - revealing the need to visualise data to check scatterplot/trends
  • A plot is a mapping from columns in your data to visual properties on your page

How data is plotted

My data Page
Estimate Position on y-axis
Population Position on x-axis
Reliability Colour
MoE Size

ggplot

ggplot(dataframe, mapping = aes(x=x, y=y) #Aesthetic mappings (assigning columns to DATA plotted) )+ #Creates a blank canvas geom_( )+ #Add aes() for columns if needed, to assign CHARACTERISTICS to the plot) #Decorations

Arguments inside aes()

  • color - assign a colour, or a column_name
  • ggplot(aes(x = reorder(NAME, estimate), y = estimate)) - reorder the NAME column by the length of estimate –> so it is in order according to size of the y (e.g. height of bar chart etc)

Potential shapes for geom_

  • point (scatterplot)
  • smooth (to add best fit line)
  • histogram (specify bins/bindwidth for best results)
  • boxplot
  • col
  • line
  • errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - moe, ymax = estimate + moe) - need set upper and lower limit for all y-values. Hence need to have the y-value AND moe for each row

Decorations

  • facet_wrap(~column_name) - to facet the plots according to a category
  • coord_flip() - to flip x and y axis, often to increase reliability
  • theme_minimal()
  • scale_y_continuous(labels = scalls::comma) - add commas to numbers with e.g. 1000 –> 1,000

Coefficient of variation (CV)

Is the relative measure of sampling error * CV = (standard_error/estimate) * 100 * SE, standard error is a standard number like 0.95 - which reflects the confidence level * MoE is based on the characteristics of the sample - e.g. size / variance of sample

Generally,

CV Reliability
Low (15%) High reliability
Medium (15-30%) Medium
High (30%) High sampling error

Derived uncertainty: How?

  • MoE for both numerator and denominator need to be derived into a new MoE
  • use function!
    • moe_sum(moe, estimate) - for adding estimates together
    • moe_prop() - for a proportion, get one estimate as share of another
    • moe_ratio() - for a ratio (of non equivalent value, unlike proportion which often operates on the same population)

How to use moe_prop()

mutate( share = below_povertyE / totalE, share_moe = moe_prop(below_povertyE, totalE, ## ORDER: estimate, estimate(denominator), moe, moe(denominator) below_povertyM, totalM) )

So how to measure uncertainty for change over time?

  • For ACS 5 it is difficult because there are a lot of overlapping intervals (e.g. 2019-2023, and 2018-2022 actually has many overlapping years)
    • Hence need to compare non-overlapping intervals like 2014-2018 and 2019-2023

Making functions for acs

get_poverty <- function(yr) {
  get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    variables = "B07012_002",
    state     = "NY",
    year      = yr,
    survey    = "acs5"
  ) %>%
    mutate(period = paste0(yr - 4, "-", yr)) # GIVES A COLUMN WITH STRING. E.G. "2014-2018", for get_poverty(2018)
}
